content:
andrew: heads-up — ran a batch of end-to-end perf sweeps against mistral-7b and mixtral variants after yesterday's kernel blacklist change. seeing a p95 regression on long-context streams when speculative decoding + draft pairing is enabled :frowning:

andrew: quick numbers from prod-like workload (seq=2048, batch=8, drafts=3, spec on):
```
p50: 42ms/token
p95: 198ms/token  <-- used to be ~92ms
p99: 410ms/token
accept_rate (speculative): 0.64  <-- down from ~0.91 baseline
```

jess: wow that p95 jump is big. is the kernel fallback path being hit? any kernel selection logs? :eyes:

andrew: yes — runtime is choosing the generic fallback GEMM path for attention at certain head/kvdim combos. the blacklist rule was added to avoid RoPE-corruption with scaled RoPE profiles, but it seems to be overbroad (affects mixtral family heads with kv_dim % 64 == 16).

runtime-bot: kernel-pick: model=mistral-7b, seq=2048, head_dim=64, kv_dim=1024, chosen_kernel=fallback_gemm, reason=ropecorrection_blacklist_match

maya: also noticed a KV-cache churn pattern in the traces. when drafts are produced from Qwen-compat drafts, tokenizer alignment differs (different BOS/space tokens) and we see a KV flip: cache invalidation + rewarm which spikes latency for the next tokens. small example in traces: last token ids differ by 1 because Qwen inserts a special <n> token.

jess: can you paste the minimal trace snippet?

andrew: pasted below — this is simplified:
```
TRACE: req=abcd1234
  step 1: model=mistral-7b, prompt_len=27, kv_cache_state=ok
  draft 1 (qwen-compat): generated tokens [502, 11, 3]  <-- tokenizer uses multi-byte BOS
  reconcile: detected token_alignment_mismatch -> invalidate_kv_cache
  step 2: rewarm kv_cache (full attention warmup) -> +120ms
```

samir: so two distinct problems: 1) kernel selection blacklist too broad (causes slow fallback path), 2) tokenizer mismatch across draft pairing causes KV invalidation and rewarm. either alone is painful, both together amplify p95.

maya: proposaled mitigations:
- relax blacklist rules: only block kernels when rope_scale != 1.0 AND head_dim is non-power-of-two. we can add a short unit test against mixtral head shapes.
- add a lightweight token_alignment check before accepting a draft: if draft tokenization prefix length differs, mark as low-confidence and lower acceptance threshold rather than invalidating whole cache.
- opportunistic partial-kv-reuse: when invalidation triggered, try suffix-only rewarm instead of full rewarm if draft divergence is at tail.

jess: any quick A/B we can run? like enable token_alignment gating only for 24h on canary traffic?

andrew: yup. I ran a micro-canary on dev cluster with token_alignment gating (no full invalidation) + relaxed blacklist. results:
```
canary (n=1200 req):
  p95: 110ms/token
  accept_rate: 0.87
  cpu_util: +3%
```

jess: that's promising. acceptance rate improved a lot and p95 cut roughly in half vs regression. what about end-to-end quality — any rejected useful drafts?

andrew: human-smoke checks show negligible quality drop; we saw a few marginal drafts that used slightly different whitespace but semantics preserved.

samir: action items:
- andrew: open PR to relax the kernel blacklist with targeted unit tests (owner + runtime infra). link when ready.
- maya: prototype token_alignment gating feature that sets per-draft acceptance adjustment and suffix-rewarm heuristic. expose metric: "spec.token_alignment_mismatch_rate"
- jess: run 48h canary split (10% traffic) with both changes and collect p50/p95/accept_rate + KL divergence on token distributions.

maya: quick patch idea (pseudocode):
```
if draft.token_prefix_len != primary.token_prefix_len:
  draft.acceptance_threshold *= 0.7
  if draft.divergence_pos > tail_threshold:
    rewarm_suffix_only()
  else:
    full_invalidate()
```

jess: also add a perf-counter where kernel fallback counts are exported per model-family so we know exactly which head/kvdim combos still hit fallback.

andrew: noted. kernel telemetry already exists but it's coarse; will add per-model-family breakdown.

runtime-bot: perf-alert: kernel-fallback-rate for mistral-7b spiked from 1.2% -> 18.4% after blacklist commit.

maya: timeline: I'll push the token_alignment gating branch today (WIP) and try to wire the new metric. andrew — will you draft the blacklist PR?

andrew: yeah I'll have a PR by EOD with tests. I'll include a small synthetic reproducer to avoid regressing RoPE fixes.

jess: thanks team. let's target canary tomorrow morning. add docs to the runbook about "kv flip" symptoms (tokenization mismatch + p95 spike) so oncall can triage quickly. :thumbsup:

samir: adding retro note — speculative decoding still gives good throughput gains when drafts and tokenizers are family-aligned. our goal: make pairing robust and fail-safe so we don't pay huge latency tax for mixed families.

andrew: +1. logging action items in the issue tracker now. will @mention folks when PRs are up.

maya: will post link to canary dashboard once metrics wired.

runtime-bot: deploy scheduled: canary split -> eng-runtime tomorrow 09:00 UTC

jess: great, closing the loop here. keep updates brief in this thread.
